Keep client/server interfaces lean and consistent: don't add a flag, option, or field that merely duplicates behavior already implied elsewhere in the contract — collapse it into the single real gate (e.g., drop a redundant `mcpApps` option once the underlying filter can be applied unconditionally per spec). Don't expose methods on a client/host interface that the underlying protocol can't actually fulfill; either implement real support or remove the method so callers aren't led to call something that silently no-ops or throws (e.g., drop `updateSessionModel` from a cloud session host when the Hub protocol has no command for it). Any field added to a request/input must be carried symmetrically through every corresponding response/event path — a value that goes in but never comes back out (e.g., `displayPrompt` missing from `pending_prompt_submitted` projections) is a trap for the next integrator, so trace and update all serialization/projection sites together. Finally, when a piece of state is derivable from an existing shared contract (e.g., provider "configured" status from `GatewayProviderMetadata`), expose it through that shared contract rather than introducing a second, independently-maintained flag in a different schema that can drift out of sync.
